---
title: "fesm_clock"
subtitle: "Run clock, cadences and output/restart schedules"
---

## Overview

`fesm_clock` is one run clock for a coupled model: integer ticks inside,
`real(dp)` years at every interface, a declared calendar. Model time is
`n` ticks (`integer(int64)`) with `N` ticks per year (`ticks_per_year`,
default 36000), so every common step (1, 0.5, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 1/12, 1/360,
1/32 yr) is a whole number of ticks. Years are never accumulated: every time
the clock returns is `n/N`, evaluated once, so `t1` of one interval is
bit-identical to `t0` of the next.

- `clock_t`: the run (`time_init`, `time_end`, `dtt`), the views of model
  time, the calendar and year length, restart state.
- `cadence_t`: "every `dt` yr" on the absolute grid `phase + k*dt` (counted
  from 0, not from `time_init`), or every step. Due once per grid time; the
  component is told the interval `[t0, t1]`.
- `schedule_t`: output or restart times (`none | const | times | file`, keys
  as in `timeout`), on the step grid, with a cursor.

Every year value (from a namelist or an argument) is converted once to ticks
and must be a whole number of ticks; every grid relation is checked at init,
so a run that starts can never miss or round a time:

| Check | Where | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Year values | every init, `clock_to_ticks` | whole number of ticks (4-ulp test), \|n\| < 2^53 |
| Step grid | `clock_init` | `dtt > 0`, `time_end > time_init`, `time_end = time_init + k*dtt`, `time_ref` whole years |
| Cadence grid on the step grid | `cadence_init` | `dt` a multiple of `dtt`, `phase` on the step grid |
| Schedule times on the step grid | `schedule_init` | times outside `[time_init, time_end]` are dropped first |
| Restart times on every cadence grid | `clock_start` | with an active restart schedule: every restart time and `time_end`; an empty intersection of the cadence grids stops |

The design note `docs/dev/clock-design.md` gives the rationale (choice of N,
precision, chunk alignment).

## Views and calendar

| `method` | `clock_time` | `clock_time_rel` (forcing time) | `clock_time_cal` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rel` | n/N | = time | time_rel + time_ref |
| `cal` | n/N | time − time_ref | = time |
| `const` | n/N | frozen at `time_const` | time_rel + time_ref |

`clock_time_elapsed` counts from the experiment start, which survives chunk
continuations. Paleo runs use `rel` with negative times (−21000 = 21 ka BP).

The calendar (`360_day`, `365_day` alias `noleap`, `none`) places the
model-time year fraction in days and months; `gregorian` and `julian` are
rejected, as their year length varies. The year length `year` (`360d`,
`365d`, `julian`, `gregorian`, `tropical`, the `sec_year_*` of
`phys_constants`) converts rates and is independent of the calendar. Neither
has a default: both are required.

## Public API

All times in and out are `real(dp)` years; ticks appear only in
`clock_to_ticks`, `clock_to_years`, `is_multiple_of_all` and restart files.
`init`, `start`, `clock_to_ticks`, the restart reads and the calendar queries
take an optional `stat` (set to 1 instead of stopping, see
[fesm_log](log.qmd)).

| Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clock_init(clk, filename, group [, defaults_file, stat])` | Keys `time_init`, `time_end`, `dtt`, `calendar`, `year` (required), `method` (`rel`), `time_ref` (1950), `ticks_per_year` (36000), and for `const` exactly one of `time_const`, `time_const_cal`. A key may come from `defaults_file` (same group). |
| `clock_init(clk, time_init, time_end, dtt, calendar, year [, method, time_const, time_const_cal, time_ref, ticks_per_year, stat])` | Same from arguments. |
| `clock_start(clk [, stat])` | Lock the registry, run the restart checks, log the table (`clock_describe`). Required before the first advance. |
| `clock_advance(clk)` | `n = n + dt`; stops if not started or finished. |
| `clock_finished(clk)`, `clock_finish(clk)` | `n >= n_end`; end early at the current step (kill switch). |
| `clock_step_index(clk)` | Steps taken in this run (`int64`). |
| `clock_time`, `clock_time_rel`, `clock_time_cal`, `clock_time_elapsed` | Views of model time. |
| `clock_time_init`, `clock_time_end`, `clock_dtt` | Run parameters. |
| `clock_to_ticks(clk, years, what [, stat])`, `clock_to_years(clk, n)`, `clock_is_representable(clk, years)` | Conversions; `what` names the value in the message. |
| `clock_year_fraction`, `clock_day_of_year`, `clock_month`, `clock_day_of_month`, `clock_sec_day` | Calendar position of model time; `clk%sec_year` [s]. With calendar `none` all but `clock_year_fraction` stop. |
| `cadence_init(c, clk, name, dt [, phase, stat])` | Every `dt` yr on `phase + k*dt`; `dt <= 0`: off. |
| `cadence_init(c, clk, name, every_step=.true. [, stat])` | Due at every step, whatever `dtt` is in this chunk. |
| `cadence_init(c, clk, name, per_year=12 [, phase, stat])` | `dt = N/12` exactly. |
| `cadence_due(c, clk)`, `cadence_mark(c, clk)` | Due: now is on the grid and not yet marked; mark after the component reached `t1`. |
| `cadence_interval(c, clk, t0, t1)` | `[last mark, now]`. |
| `cadence_t_last`, `cadence_t_next`, `cadence_dt_years` | Last mark, next grid time, `dt` [yr]. |
| `schedule_init(s, clk, name, filename, group [, restart, defaults_file, stat])` | Keys `method`, and `dt` (`const`), `times` (one string of values and `t0:dt:t1` ranges), `file` (lines of the same, `#` comments). |
| `schedule_init(s, clk, name [, dt=, times=, restart, stat])` | Same from arguments (`dt > 0`: `const`; neither: `none`). |
| `schedule_due(s, clk)`, `schedule_t_next`, `schedule_times`, `schedule_size` | Now is a scheduled time (or the run is finished); next time; all times; count. |
| `is_multiple_of_all(n, cadences)`, `clock_restart_allowed(clk)` | `n` / now on the grid of every cadence. |
| `clock_restart_write(clk, file)`, `clock_restart_read(clk, file [, stat])` | Clock state; read sets `clk%continued`. |
| `cadence_restart_write(c, file)`, `cadence_restart_read(c, clk, file [, stat])` | Cadence state, keyed by name; read after the clock. |
| `clock_describe(clk)` | The schedule table, through `log_msg`. |

An output schedule includes `time_init` (`const`; `times`/`file` if listed)
and always `time_end`; a restart schedule excludes `time_init`. `const`
lists the absolute multiples of `dt`. After `clock_finish`, every output
schedule is due once; a restart schedule only if `clock_restart_allowed`,
otherwise the skipped bundle is logged with the offending cadence.

## Example

The driver loop of a coupled model (namelist groups `ctrl`, `tm_2D`,
`tm_rst`):

```fortran
use fesm_clock

call clock_init(clk, path_par, "ctrl")
call cadence_init(c_ice, clk, "ice", every_step=.true.)
call cadence_init(c_geo, clk, "geo", dt=10.0_dp)
call schedule_init(s_2D,  clk, "out_2D",  path_par, "tm_2D")
call schedule_init(s_rst, clk, "restart", path_par, "tm_rst", restart=.true.)
if (restart /= "None") call run_restore(restart, dom, clk, c_ice, c_geo)
call clock_start(clk)                                   ! validate, log the table

do
    if (schedule_due(s_2D, clk))  call write_2D(dom, clock_time(clk))
    if (schedule_due(s_rst, clk)) call run_restart_write(dom, clk, c_ice, c_geo)
    if (clock_finished(clk)) exit

    call clock_advance(clk)
    call forcing_update(frc, clock_time_rel(clk))

    if (cadence_due(c_geo, clk)) then
        call cadence_interval(c_geo, clk, t0, t1)
        call geo_update(dom%geo, t0, t1)                ! integrates [t0, t1]
        call cadence_mark(c_geo, clk)
    end if
    if (cadence_due(c_ice, clk)) then
        call ice_update(dom%ice, clock_time(clk))
        call cadence_mark(c_ice, clk)
    end if
end do
```

`run_restore` calls `clock_restart_read` and then `cadence_restart_read` for
each cadence; `run_restart_write` the two writes. With

```
&ctrl
    method    = "rel"
    time_init = -21000
    time_end  = 0
    dtt       = 5
    calendar  = "365_day"
    year      = "tropical"
/
&tm_2D
    method = "const"
    dt     = 1000
/
&tm_rst
    method = "const"
    dt     = 5000
/
```

`clock_start` logs

```
INFO  fesm_clock: rel, model time -21000.0 -> 0.0 yr, dtt = 5 yr (4200 steps)
    forcing  time_rel = model time; time_cal = time_rel + 1950
    calendar 365_day; year = tropical (31556926.08 s); tick = 1/36000 yr
    elapsed  origin -21000.0 (this run)
    name      kind     dt [yr]   phase  first     last      count
    ice       cadence  step      -      -20995.0  0.0       4200
    geo       cadence  10        0      -20990.0  0.0       2100
    out_2D    output   1000      0      -21000.0  0.0       22
    restart   restart  5000      0      -20000.0  0.0       5
    restart grid: every 10 yr from 0 (geo)
```

A value that is not a whole number of ticks, or off a grid, stops at init
with the nearest valid values:

```
fesm:: error in fesm_clock::cadence_init
    cadence "geo": dt is not a whole number of ticks.
    dt = 0.3333 yr, 1 tick = 1/36000 yr (dt = 11998.8 ticks)
    nearest representable: 0.33327778 yr (11998 ticks), 0.33330556 yr (11999 ticks)
    1/3 yr is a whole number of ticks: write it with 16 significant digits, 0.3333333333333333
    for thirds of a year use per_year = 3
  stopped by fesm_error.
```

## Chunks and restarts

Because the grids are absolute, a chain of chunks (`time_init` = previous
`time_end`) fires every cadence and output at the times of one long run,
whatever `dtt` each chunk uses. `clock_restart_read` detects a
**continuation** when the bundle time equals `time_init` (`continued =
.true.`, the elapsed origin is kept, cadences restore their last mark) and a
**branch** otherwise (elapsed origin and last marks reset to `time_init`).
The bundle holds `clock_ticks_per_year`, `clock_n`, `clock_n_origin`,
`clock_dtt` and `cadence_<name>_{n_last,dt,phase}` as `dp` scalars (exact for
\|n\| < 2^53; ncio has no `int64`) and the attribute `clock_method`; a
bundle written at another N is converted exactly or rejected.

`fesm_clock` is independent of `timestepping` (`tstep_class`) and `timeout`,
which are unchanged.

Test: `make check-clock` (nine programs in `test/clock/`).
